title: Pay Off Debt or Save First? The Order That Works

lines.say: Pay off debt, or save first?
It's the question everyone asks. The answer is: both, in a specific order. Here's the order, and the math behind each step.
Five steps.
Step one. A starter emergency fund.

scene.label: Starter emergency fund
scene.sub: one month of bills, from episode one

lines.cap: Before you attack debt, save one month of bills. In our example, $2,371. Without it, the next car repair goes right back on the card, and you pay off the same debt twice.
lines.say: Before you attack debt, save one month of bills. In our example, twenty-three seventy-one. Without it, the next car repair goes right back on the card, and you're paying off the same debt twice.
Step two. Grab any employer match.

scene.text: An employer match is an instant return.

lines.say: If your employer matches retirement contributions, that's often the best return you'll ever see. Say they match fifty cents per dollar, up to six percent of pay.

scene.foot: per dollar, per year · plans vary, check yours

lines.cap: On $60,000, 6% is $3,600 a year from you, and $1,800 from your employer. An instant 50% return. Even a 24% card can't beat that.
lines.say: On sixty thousand, six percent is thirty-six hundred a year from you, and eighteen hundred from your employer. An instant fifty percent return. Even a twenty-four percent card can't beat that.
Plans vary, so check yours.
Step three. Kill high-interest debt.

scene.label: Paying off a 24% card
scene.sub: a guaranteed return, no savings account comes close

lines.cap: Credit cards, store cards, anything around 10% or more. Every dollar here earns a guaranteed return equal to the rate. Episodes 2 and 11 have the plans.
lines.say: Credit cards, store cards, anything around ten percent or more. Every dollar here earns a guaranteed return equal to the rate. Episodes two and eleven have the plans.
Step four. Finish the emergency fund.

lines.cap: Now build it to 3–6 months of essentials. In our example, 3 months is $9,033. Episode 10 shows how.
lines.say: Now build it to three to six months of essentials. In our example, three months is nine thousand and thirty-three. Episode ten shows how.
Step five. Then decide: lower-interest debt, or saving for bigger goals.

lines.cap: A car loan at 7% versus savings at 4%? Paying the loan earns more. But savings stays flexible. With low-rate debt it's a judgment call, and both are good choices.
lines.say: A car loan at seven percent versus savings at four? Paying the loan earns more. But savings stays flexible. With low-rate debt, it's a judgment call, and both are good choices.

scene.head: THE ORDER
items: Starter fund: one month of bills
Then: low-rate debt or bigger goals

lines.say: Recap.
Starter fund. Employer match.
Kill high-interest debt. Finish the emergency fund.
Then choose your goals.
